ATL.name: Jock Landale
ATL.note: Landale (hip) is out for Sunday's game against Bucks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
ATL.long: Landale missed four games earlier this month with a left hip issue, and he'll sit out Sunday due to right hip inflammation. Look for Zuby Ejiofor to see more minutes behind starter Onyeke Okongwu with Landale out of commission Sunday.

ATL.name: Kingston Flemings
ATL.note: Flemings (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bucks.
ATL.long: Flemings left Friday's 125-117 loss to Chicago with back tightness after playing 17 minutes. The ailment will keep the rookie first-rounder on the sidelines Sunday, with veteran CJ McCollum the likely candidate to join the starting lineup. Flemings' next chance to suit up will come Wednesday versus Oklahoma City.

ATL.name: Mouhamed Gueye
ATL.note: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
ATL.long: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

ATL.name: Asa Newell
ATL.note: Newell (toe) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Chicago.
ATL.long: Newell will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left great toe hyperextension. He can be considered week-to-week until the Hawks provide an update on his progress.

ATL.name: Henri Veesaar
ATL.note: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
ATL.long: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

CHA.name: Kon Knueppel
CHA.note: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
CHA.long: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

CHA.name: Dennis Schroder
CHA.note: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
CHA.long: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

CHI.name: Tobe Awaka
CHI.note: Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Cavaliers.
CHI.long: Awaka will miss a fourth consecutive game due a disc irritation in his back. His next chance to suit up will come against the Nets on Wednesday.

CHI.name: Jalen Smith
CHI.note: Smith (finger) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Cleveland.
CHI.long: Smith didn't play in Saturday's 117-106 win over Minnesota. Nic Claxton (hamstring) also didn't suit up in that one, resulting in Zach Collins getting the start. Claxton is good to go for Monday's meeting with the Cavaliers, so he will likely start if Smith doesn't get on the floor.

CHI.name: Caleb Wilson
CHI.note: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
CHI.long: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

CLE.name: Jaylon Tyson
CLE.note: Tyson (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against the Bulls.
CLE.long: Tyson is questionable to play due to right ankle injury management. The third-year wing missed six games with the ailment but has appeared in three consecutive outings, including a Friday and Saturday night back-to-back in which he played a combined 64 minutes. If he is sidelined Monday, Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas will all get increased burn.

CLE.name: Peyton Watson
CLE.note: Watson (abdominal soreness) is questionable to play in Monday's game against the Bulls.
CLE.long: Watson missed Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas due to a hamstring injury, but he's now dealing with right abdominal soreness. Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas will see an uptick in minutes if Watson remains sidelined Monday.

CLE.name: Evan Mobley
CLE.note: Mobley (toe) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Chicago.
CLE.long: Mobley will miss a third consecutive game due to a left big toe sprain. Jaylon Tyson (ankle) and Peyton Watson (abdominal soreness) are both questionable to play, so if either of them was to miss the home tilt versus Chicago, Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas would stand to see increased burn.

CLE.name: Sam Merrill
CLE.note: Merrill (elbow) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bulls.
CLE.long: Merrill is set to miss his sixth consecutive game due to a right elbow injury. With the majority of the Cavs' starting lineup expected to return versus Chicago, Tyrese Proctor and Meleek Thomas should continue to see the majority of Merrill's vacated minutes in the backcourt.

CLE.name: Nae'Qwan Tomlin
CLE.note: Tomlin is set to miss several weeks with a lower back stress reaction, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
CLE.long: This is a tough blow for the forward and there's no guarantee he's cleared right away when he's re-evaluated in three-to-four weeks. Tomlin wasn't projected to crack the rotation ahead of Opening Night and was penciled in to be an emergency depth option.

DAL.name: Max Christie
DAL.note: Christie (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
DAL.long: Christie will miss a second consecutive game due to sprained left ankle. With Kyrie Irving (knee) also out for Dallas, Naji Marshall, Zaccharie Risacher and Walter Clayton Jr. will help fill the vacated minutes in the backcourt.

DAL.name: Santi Aldama
DAL.note: Aldama (ankle) is out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
DAL.long: Aldama will miss Sunday's game with an ankle injury, which is not surprising given it is the second half of a back-to-back set. Morez Johnson could see extra minutes with Aldama out.

DAL.name: Kyrie Irving
DAL.note: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
DAL.long: Irving was listed as questionable to face Boston after playing 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss in Cleveland. He will, however, sit out the second leg of the back-to-back for Dallas, which will likely send Cooper Flagg's usage to the moon. Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton Jr. should also get a boost in minutes and playmaking responsibilities off the bench.

DAL.name: Dereck Lively II
DAL.note: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Thursday's game in Minnesota.
DAL.long: Lively is still working his way back from foot surgery. He's reportedly trending favorably, though he should continue to be classified as week-to-week, at least until the team provides an update. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford is expected to stay in the starting lineup, with Morez Johnson (shin), Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse all in line to spend time at the five when needed.

DAL.name: Tarik Biberovic
DAL.note: Biberovic (heel) is out for Thursday's game against Minnesota.
DAL.long: Biberovic remains plagued by right heel bursitis. The rookie forward carries no timetable for his season debut.

DAL.name: Sergio de Larrea
DAL.note: De Larrea (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game at Minnesota.
DAL.long: De Larrea hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a right knee sprain, but he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Still, he can be considered week-to-week until Dallas provides an update on his progress.

DEN.name: Julian Strawther
DEN.note: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
DEN.long: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

DET.name: Duncan Robinson
DET.note: Robinson (thigh) did not return to Saturday's 137-117 win over the Pistons. He finished with 10 points (3-8 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist across 17 minutes.
DET.long: There haven't been any updates regarding the severity of Robinson's injury. However, he shouldn't be considered a lock to suit up against the Spurs on Tuesday night. If Robinson is unavailable for that contest, Ronald Holland and Kevin Huerter are candidates to receive more playing time, with one of those players potentially moving into the starting lineup.

DET.name: Ugonna Onyenso
DET.note: Onyenso agreed to a two-way contract with the Pistons on Thursday.
DET.long: The No. 53 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Onyenso appears poised to see run in the G League after putting pen to paper on a two-way deal. He'll likely face an uphill battle to carve out a role in the rotation, so Detroit will presumably allow him to continue his development with Motor City.

DET.name: Isaiah Joe
DET.note: Joe (hip) is out for Monday against the Wizards.
DET.long: Joe is missing a seventh consecutive contest with a bruised hip. His next chance to play comes Thursday in a road rematch with Washington.

DET.name: Jalen Duren
DET.note: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
DET.long: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

GSW.name: Gui Santos
GSW.note: Santos is questionable for Monday's game against New Orleans due to right ankle inflammation.
GSW.long: Santos appears to have put a lingering knee injury behind him, but he's now experiencing an issue with his right ankle. He'll presumably test the injury in shootaround and pregame to determine whether he can suit up for Monday's game.

GSW.name: Stephen Curry
GSW.note: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

GSW.name: Brandon Williams
GSW.note: Williams (hamstring) will miss at least one week, per Anthony Slater of ESPN.com.
GSW.long: Williams has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain in the aftermath of Monday's game against the Pelicans, and his status for Golden State's upcoming five-game road trip is in serious doubt. With Williams facing an extended absence, the Warriors are likely to lean more on De'Anthony Melton in the backourt.

GSW.name: Kristaps Porzingis
GSW.note: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
GSW.long: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

GSW.name: Moses Moody
GSW.note: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

GSW.name: Jimmy Butler III
GSW.note: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
GSW.long: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

HOU.name: Fred VanVleet
HOU.note: VanVleet (right knee injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
HOU.long: VanVleet will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday at Miami. With the veteran floor general sidelined, Reed Sheppard, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Bruce Thornton are candidates for increased playing time, while Amen Thompson figures to see increased on-ball duties.

HOU.name: Clint Capela
HOU.note: Capela (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Washington.
HOU.long: Capela is trending toward a return to action, though he'll remain sidelined Sunday due to a right ankle sprain. His next chance to suit up will come Monday at Miami.

HOU.name: Marcus Smart
HOU.note: Smart has been suspended three games for throwing a punch during Wednesday's matchup against Golden State, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
HOU.long: Smart, who was ejected from Wednesday's game for punching Charles Bassey, will begin serving his suspension Friday night against the Jazz, meaning he'll be eligible to return Wednesday versus Indiana. Bruce Thornton and Reed Sheppard should be in line for more minutes while Smart serves his three-game ban.

IND.name: Andrew Nembhard
IND.note: Nembhard (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 76ers, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
IND.long: Nembhard will miss his third contest of the season due to left hip soreness. T.J. McConnell should slide into the first unit while Quenton Jackson gets a boost in minutes off the bench.

IND.name: Tyrese Haliburton
IND.note: Head coach Rick Carlisle said Wednesday that Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least 10 more days, Alex Golden of SI.com reports.
IND.long: Haliburton is still recovering from a left hamstring strain and will need more time to ramp up. Andrew Nembhard should continue seeing increased on-ball duties in Haliburton's stead, while Quenton Jackson and Braden Smith are also candidates for increased burn.

IND.name: Johnny Furphy
IND.note: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
IND.long: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

IND.name: Ben Sheppard
IND.note: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
IND.long: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

LAC.name: Brandon Ingram
LAC.note: Ingram (Achilles) won't play in Friday's game against the Thunder, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
LAC.long: Ingram is ramping up his activity as he nears his season debut for the Clippers, but he's not yet cleared for game action amid his Achilles rehab. Until the star forward is ready to suit up, Kris Dunn, Rui Hachimura and Derrick Jones should all hang onto starting roles.

LAC.name: Yanic Konan Niederhauser
LAC.note: Niederhauser (foot) is out for Tuesday's game against Phoenix, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
LAC.long: Niederhauser has yet to make an appearance this season for the Clippers while rehabbing from foot surgery. It's unclear at this time when he'll be available to take the court, and he can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

LAC.name: Bradley Beal
LAC.note: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
LAC.long: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

LAC.name: Jordan Miller
LAC.note: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
LAC.long: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

LAL.name: Austin Reaves
LAL.note: Reaves (heel) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Suns, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports.
LAL.long: Reaves is dealing with a left heel bruise he sustained during Wednesday's 123-112 victory over Milwaukee, and he'll now miss his second contest of the season. Luka Doncic will carry the load on offense, while Collin Sexton, Jaden Hardy and Ziaire Williams should see a boost in minutes.

MEM.name: GG Jackson
MEM.note: Jackson (foot) is out for Monday's game against Washington.
MEM.long: The Grizzlies reported Saturday that Jackson suffered a "relatively serious" injury, so it's not a shock that he won't be on the floor for Monday's matchup. However, the team has yet to provide additional clarification on the injury. Jackson can be considered doubtful for Wednesday's game in Cleveland until more information surfaces.

MEM.name: Isaiah Stewart
MEM.note: Stewart is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards due to an illness.
MEM.long: Stewart has started the last two games for Memphis, but he could miss Monday's game due to an illness. If he is unavailable, Taylor Hendricks could see extra minutes.

MEM.name: Ty Jerome
MEM.note: Jerome (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Wizards.
MEM.long: Jerome will miss a second straight matchup while nursing right hip soreness. Cam Spencer could receive another chance to start at point guard in Jerome's absence. The Virginia product's next opportunity to return will arrive Wednesday in Cleveland.

MEM.name: Quinten Post
MEM.note: Post (concussion) is questionable for Monday's game against the Wizards.
MEM.long: Post could miss a fourth consecutive game due to a concussion. Zach Edey (ankle) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) have also been deemed questionable, so Taylor Hendricks could see an expanded role.

MEM.name: Zach Edey
MEM.note: Edey (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against Washington.
MEM.long: Edey is in danger of missing a third straight matchup as he works back from a left ankle injury. The team should have another update on his availability as tipoff approaches.

MEM.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
MEM.note: Pippen (back) remains out for Wednesday's game against Denver, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
MEM.long: With Pippen set to miss another game, Memphis will continue to operate without one of its backcourt reserves. He has now been sidelined for six straight contests due to the back issue and can be considered week-to-week until Memphis offers an update on his recovery. Cam Spencer remains worth streaming in most fantasy leagues.

MEM.name: Richie Saunders
MEM.note: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
MEM.long: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

MIA.name: Pelle Larsson
MIA.note: Larsson (illness) is questionable to play in Monday's game against the Rockets.
MIA.long: Larsson has missed the last two games due to an illness, and he's in jeopardy of sitting out a third straight with the ailment. His status in practice tomorrow should clear things up prior to tipoff.

MIL.name: Ryan Rollins
MIL.note: Rollins (illness) is out for Sunday's game against the Hawks.
MIL.long: Rollins will miss his first game of the season due to an illness. Gary Trent, AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis are candidates for increased roles with Rollins sidelined.

MIL.name: Ousmane Dieng
MIL.note: Dieng will undergo a procedure to repair a fractured left finger Monday, Justin Garcia of the Milwaukee Bucks Radio Network reports.
MIL.long: Dieng was recently diagnosed with a fractured left finger, and the team has determined that he'll need to go under the knife to repair the injury. Milwaukee has yet to provide a timeline for his return, though more information should become available following the procedure.

MIN.name: Jaylen Clark
MIN.note: Clark (hamstring) has been ruled out for the next two weeks.
MIN.long: Clark suffered a right hamstring strain during Saturday's 117-106 loss to Chicago. He played three minutes as a result of the injury, and he's now slated to miss at least two weeks and will be re-evaluated at that time. Terrence Shannon Jr. and Bones Hyland will see increased playing time off the bench in Clark's absence.

MIN.name: Anthony Edwards
MIN.note: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
MIN.long: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

MIN.name: Donte DiVincenzo
MIN.note: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
MIN.long: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

NOP.name: Bryce McGowens
NOP.note: McGowens (elbow) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Warriors.
NOP.long: McGowens will miss a third consecutive outing due to an infection in his left elbow. Jaron Pierre Jr. will continue earning extra minutes off the Pelicans' bench with McGowens and Bennedict Mathurin (foot) both sidelined.

NOP.name: Bennedict Mathurin
NOP.note: Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Warriors.
NOP.long: Mathurin will miss a second straight game and his third over the last four outings due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot. Jordan Poole and Jaron Pierre Jr. will continue to get extended run with Mathurin on the shelf.

NOP.name: Trey Murphy III
NOP.note: Murphy (knees) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Golden State.
NOP.long: Murphy is set to miss a fifth consecutive game while he works his way back from bilateral patellar tendinopathy. His next chance to suit up will come against the Pistons on Wednesday. Saddiq Bey will likely remain in the starting unit for as long as Murphy is sidelined.

NOP.name: Trendon Watford
NOP.note: Watford (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Golden State.
NOP.long: Watford will miss a fifth consecutive contest due to a right ankle sprain. He remains without a clear return timetable.

NOP.name: Dejounte Murray
NOP.note: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
NOP.long: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

OKC.name: Jaylin Williams
OKC.note: Williams (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Kings.
OKC.long: Williams will miss a sixth straight contest due to lower-back spasms and is still without a timetable to return. Isaiah Hartenstein, Kenrich Williams and rookie Aday Mara will continue holding down the frontcourt for as long as Williams is sidelined.

OKC.name: Thomas Sorber
OKC.note: Sorber (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
OKC.long: Sorber is still recovering from knee surgery and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Thunder offer an update on his status.

OKC.name: Cason Wallace
OKC.note: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
OKC.long: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

OKC.name: Chet Holmgren
OKC.note: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
OKC.long: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

OKC.name: Jalen Williams
OKC.note: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
OKC.long: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

ORL.name: Jonathan Isaac
ORL.note: Isaac (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Celtics.
ORL.long: Isaac's 2026-27 season debut will have to wait, as he's still working his way back from a left knee injury. He should be considered week-to-week until Orlando provides a clear update for his return.

ORL.name: Noah Penda
ORL.note: Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
ORL.long: Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

ORL.name: Paolo Banchero
ORL.note: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
ORL.long: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

ORL.name: Izaiyah Nelson
ORL.note: Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com.
ORL.long: With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.

PHI.name: Joel Embiid
PHI.note: Embiid (right foot injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pacers.
PHI.long: Embiid will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set. With Adem Bona (back) and Dominick Barlow (back) sidelined, Dean Wade, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall could all see increased playing time, while LeBron James could also see more time at the five as well.

PHI.name: Dominick Barlow
PHI.note: Barlow (back) participated in Thursday's shootaround but doesn't have a timeline to return to game action, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
PHI.long: Barlow has been dealing with back soreness dating back to the preseason, so his participation in shootaround is an encouraging step. However, the 76ers have yet to provide a firm return date, and he'll likely need to ramp up further before he's cleared to play. Barlow should be monitored in deeper formats, but he isn't someone who needs to be rostered while he remains sidelined.

PHI.name: Adem Bona
PHI.note: Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
PHI.long: The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

PHI.name: Ariel Hukporti
PHI.note: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
PHI.long: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

PHX.name: Drew Timme
PHX.note: The Suns claimed Timme off waivers Monday, per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com.
PHX.long: After being let go by Minnesota on Saturday, Timme wasn't allowed to go through waivers unclaimed without Phoenix snatching him up. With Mark Williams (shoulder) likely out through the All-Star break, Timme helps reinforce Phoenix's depth at center.

PHX.name: Mark Williams
PHX.note: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
PHX.long: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

POR.name: Chris Youngblood
POR.note: Youngblood (foot) is out for Monday's game against the Timberwolves.
POR.long: Youngblood will miss a third straight game due to a right foot bone bruise. His next opportunity to suit up comes Tuesday against the Timberwolves.

POR.name: Vit Krejci
POR.note: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
POR.long: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

POR.name: Ja Morant
POR.note: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
POR.long: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

POR.name: Shaedon Sharpe
POR.note: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
POR.long: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

SAC.name: Zach LaVine
SAC.note: LaVine is out for Sunday's game against Oklahoma City due to illness, Brandon Rahbar of DailyThunder.com reports.
SAC.long: LaVine was ruled out shortly before tipoff after falling ill. Emanuel Sharp and Malik Monk should be in line for additional opportunities Sunday with LaVine sidelined.

SAC.name: De'Andre Hunter
SAC.note: Hunter (hip) is out for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
SAC.long: Hunter was added to the injury report close to tipoff, and he's since been downgraded to out. The Kings will be forced to play shorthanded Sunday, as Precious Achiuwa (ankle) and Zach LaVine (illness) are also unavailable. The absence of three starters should open up minutes for Leaky Black, Emanuel Sharp, Keegan Murray and Malik Monk.

SAC.name: Precious Achiuwa
SAC.note: Achiuwa (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder, Brenden Nunes of KHTK Sactown Sports 1140 reports.
SAC.long: Achiuwa is battling with ankle soreness and will miss a second straight game while on the mend. Keegan Murray drew the start in Achiuwa's absence Friday and is a good candidate to do so again Sunday evening.

SAC.name: Maxime Raynaud
SAC.note: Raynaud (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Thunder.
SAC.long: Raynaud will miss his 13th consecutive game to start 2026-27 after injuring his knee during the preseason. It sounds like the Frenchman is getting closer to making his season debut, with his next chance to do so coming Wednesday versus Phoenix.

SAC.name: Ben Simmons
SAC.note: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
SAC.long: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

SAS.name: De'Aaron Fox
SAS.note: Fox (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
SAS.long: Fox has been dealing with left hip tightness recently, and it will finally force him to miss his first game of the season. He's playing 28.6 minutes a night, the lowest since his 27.8 mark during his rookie campaign in 2017, en route to averages of 13.6 points, 4.4 rebounds, 5.8 assists, 1.3 steals and 1.0 three-pointers across 13 games in 2026-27. Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper will handle the playmaking duties, while Julian Champagnie would be the top candidate to start in place of Fox.

SAS.name: Tobias Harris
SAS.note: Harris (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Chicago, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
SAS.long: With Harris still sidelined, San Antonio will rely more on Julian Champagnie. Harris has yet to make his Spurs debut this season, so his absence continues to leave minutes available on the wing until he is cleared to return.

SAS.name: Jayden Quaintance
SAS.note: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
SAS.long: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

TOR.name: Nate Bittle
TOR.note: Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Knicks, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet.ca reports.
TOR.long: Bittle is still working his way back from a foot fracture that has plagued him for multiple months, and he remains without a clear return timeline. He can be considered week-to-week for the time being.

TOR.name: Kevin McCullar Jr.
TOR.note: McCullar signed a two-way contract with the Raptors on Thursday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
TOR.long: McCullar quickly finds a new home after being waived by the Knicks in late October. The forward is expected to play a prominent role for Toronto's G League affiliate.

TOR.name: Kawhi Leonard
TOR.note: Head coach Darko Rajakovic said Wednesday that Leonard (knee) is doing individual on-court work and is progressing well, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
TOR.long: The Raptors are expected to provide another update on Leonard's status in about one week, though it's encouraging to see how he's progressed thus far. Collin Murray-Boyles and Ja'Kobe Walter are candidates for increased playing time for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

UTA.name: Jaxson Hayes
UTA.note: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Spurs.
UTA.long: Hayes left Friday's game against the Rockets with the knee issue, and it will now sideline him for Sunday's tilt versus San Antonio. Mo Bamba will likely join the starting unit while Tony Bradley and Kyle Filipowski should earn more playing time off the bench.

UTA.name: Trey Alexander
UTA.note: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
UTA.long: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

UTA.name: Lauri Markkanen
UTA.note: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
UTA.long: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

UTA.name: Jusuf Nurkic
UTA.note: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
UTA.long: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

UTA.name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
UTA.note: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
UTA.long: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

WAS.name: Tre Johnson
WAS.note: Johnson (back) won't play in Sunday's game against Houston, Josh Robbins of The Athletic reports.
WAS.long: Johnson is battling a sore back, so he will miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign. Without him, Bub Carrington and Will Riley are candidates for more minutes.

WAS.name: Tristan Vukcevic
WAS.note: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Detroit.
WAS.long: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip impingement. The big man can be viewed as week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

WAS.name: Reece Beekman
WAS.note: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
WAS.long: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

WAS.name: Justin Champagnie
WAS.note: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
WAS.long: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

WAS.name: Jamir Watkins
WAS.note: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
WAS.long: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.
